bare.rule: Start with a hidden score of 0. Insult decreases the score by 1, apologise increases it by 1, and gift increases it by 1. At the end, the mood is warm if the score is greater than 0, otherwise cold.

random answers.rule: Ignore gifts. Let I be the number of insults and A the number of apologies. If the last action is an insult, the mood is cold. Otherwise, the mood is warm only if A > I; if A <= I, it is cold.

rounds.rule: Robin starts at a neutral tie; apologies count +1, insults count -1, gifts are ignored, and Robin is warm only when the net score is positive (i.e., apologies outnumber insults).

commitments.why: If four gifts leave Robin warm, gifts must affect mood, contradicting the rule that only apologies and insults matter.
If two gifts make Robin warm, gifts are not neutral.
If a single gift makes Robin warm, gifts are not neutral or the starting tie is not cold.
Ignoring the gift leaves one insult and one apology, a tie; if warm, the gift is doing work or ties are warm.
Ignoring the gift leaves a tie; if warm, the gift is not neutral or the tie is not cold.
